title: Best Grading Company for Sports Cards (2026)
verdict: The best grading company for sports cards in 2026 is AGS when you want an exact, documented grade, and PSA when the card is headed to auction.

Send the card you will auction to PSA if the premium covers its fee. Send the rest of your sports cards somewhere fast and flat-priced. That is the split most sellers land on, and AGS fits the second job.

list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.
A permanent online record, reachable by cert number or shared link.
Surface: scratches, print lines and dimples.
Whether the card is standard size. AGS does not take jumbos.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.
Most cards qualify. AGS grades TCG and sports, old and new, signed, miscut and error cards, and does not turn away damaged cards unless they are illegible. It does not take jumbo sizes.

faq.q: What is the best grading company for sports cards?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on sports cards at a flat $18. PSA for the strongest resale on key rookies. SGC for vintage.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.
Yes: basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, including chrome finishes. Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate, or $18, $23 and $33 on the bulk tiers.

Signed cards are accepted for grading. If you need the autograph itself authenticated, use a grader that sells that service. Beckett lists a $5 autograph add-on, and CGC offers autograph authentication.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.
